entries.note: The shipment's status: Expeditors delivered the freight and closed its service.

entries.wording: Services Completed: Turned Over to Client Trucker
entries.note: The shipment's status: Expeditors handed the freight to the trucker its client sent and closed its service, so nothing follows on its side.
A shipment status and a status change: a trucker was told to collect the freight for its last leg.
The shipment's status while Expeditors waits for information it needs to go on.
The status change that put the shipment on hold for a reason other than credit.
A status change that does not say whose dispatch took the freight; the shipment's status beside it says whether Expeditors' service ended.
The supplier asked Expeditors to book the shipment.
A leg was booked. Onward legs are booked after the freight has moved, which the shared late-registration reading keeps from stepping back.
The customs broker at destination was told of the shipment, sometimes before it leaves its origin; it states no movement or customs step.
Expeditors has the freight, but not yet its documents.
The import declaration was submitted; the release is still to come.
Comes with the declaration, days before the release in one sample, so it is no release.
The container left the port terminal towards Expeditors' warehouse, not the consignee.
A slot was booked for a pickup or delivery; nothing moved.
The freight reached the destination station; its delivery is still to come.
The empty container went back to the shipping line after it was unloaded; it says nothing new about the freight.
